column1: # The job state vocabulary the shipping server stores and the two vocabularies
# it publishes from it, the old backlog. No section of earlier research covers
# jobs, and earlier research names five values where there are eight
# stored and six published.
# Columns: the stored state, what ConnectJobState publishes, what
# LifeTimeJobState publishes, whether the state is terminal, and what this
# adapter's connectJobState answers for the same input. A core answer of - is a
# state this adapter publishes nothing for.
# The stored half was read from ./data/state.db on a run of the retired server
# on 2026-08-29: printer_jobs.state is a TEXT column and printer_jobs carries
# uuid, printer_uuid, state, file_path, file_name, progress, time_printing,
# start_time, end_time, created_at, printer_job_id, external_context and source.
# With no job on the printer, GET /api/printers/{id}/jobs answered 200 with an
# empty array and GET /api/printers/{id}/jobs/current answered 404 with
# {"error":"no active job"}.
# The divergence in the last column is the point of this file. The shipping
# server publishes UNKNOWN on the frozen jobs/{id}/data/state channel for a job
# that is queued or downloading, and this adapter publishes nothing. A
# subscriber that reads the channel to mean "there is a job and it has not
# started" loses that. The old backlog owns the decision.
QUEUED
DOWNLOADING
PRINTING
PAUSED
FINISHED
FAILED
STOPPED
ABANDONED
